I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of.

Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does.

Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.
---AGENTS---
# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

content.text:
The runtime expects either static index.html or Vite. For a Three.js game, easiest is static HTML with importmap using CDN? But network may be restricted at runtime/browser. Better to vendor three.js locally. We can npm install three and use Vite, or simply copy three.module.js into vendor folder and use importmap.

We need a high-quality polished game. Let's design:

**"CUBECRAFT" / "Voxel Forge"** — a Minecraft-style voxel building game in Three.js.

Features:
- First-person or third-person? Mobile needs touch controls. Minecraft-style: first-person walk with joystick + look drag, plus block place/break.
- "Realistic only cubes" — meaning all geometry is cubes (voxel), with realistic materials/lighting/textures. So no non-cube meshes. Use procedural textures (canvas-generated pixel textures) for grass, dirt, stone, wood, leaves, sand, water, glass, bricks, etc. Realistic lighting: sun, sky, ambient occlusion via vertex colors, shadows, fog, water transparency. Maybe sky gradient (that's okay, background not geometry).
- World: procedurally generated terrain (cubes) with hills, trees, water, sand. Chunked greedy-ish meshing? Need performance. Simpler: instanced rendering per block type, but for editing and AO, use chunk geometry with merged faces + face culling + vertex AO. That's doable and high quality.

Given "realistic only cubes", ensure no cylinders/spheres. Use cube-based clouds, cube sun/moon? Sun can be square. Player model maybe not visible in first person. Hand? A cube block in hand? Could show held block cube.

Menu:
- Title screen with logo, buttons: Play, Settings, Controls/How to play, maybe Continue.
- Settings: graphics quality (render distance, shadows, FOV), audio volume (procedural sounds maybe), controls (sensitivity, invert Y, left-handed?), language? Keep sensible: Graphics, Audio, Controls, Gameplay. Persist to localStorage.
- Pause menu (Esc): Resume, Settings, Save, Reset world, Main menu.
- HUD: crosshair, hotbar with 9 block slots, block names, coordinates/FPS, day-night clock maybe.
- World save/load via localStorage (blocks diffs), seed.
- Mobile: virtual joystick left, look drag right, jump button, place/break buttons, hotbar touch; responsive UI.
- Tablet/PC adapt.
- Creative building: infinite blocks, break/place, block picker.
- Day/night cycle with sun/moon cubes, dynamic sky colors, stars (small cubes/points? points aren't cubes... could use tiny cube sprites instanced). "only cubes" - stars can be tiny square sprites, acceptable (still square).
- Sound: WebAudio procedural footsteps/place/break, ambient. Optional.

Quality bar: high. Need screenshot verification with playwright. Use the capture script with CAPTURE_URL etc. Need start server via start.sh (tmux). We can run `bash start.sh` maybe uses RUNTIME_DIR default-start, port 3000. AGENTS says use tmux persistent. Let's set up.

Implementation plan:
- package.json with vite + three.
- index.html
- src/main.js, src/world.js, src/player.js, src/ui.js, src/textures.js, src/audio.js, src/settings.js, style.css.

But complexity. Could do a single-page static site with ES modules and vendored three. Vite is supported and handles build. Use npm install three vite. Then `npm run build` and start.sh default-start does build itself. For local preview, use `npm run dev -- --host` maybe; or use start.sh in tmux which builds and serves on 3000.

Let's check network for npm.

Design details:

**Voxel engine**
- World size: 96x96? Render distance configurable. Chunk size 16, world height 48. Use chunk meshes with BufferGeometry (positions, normals, uv, color for AO/light).
- Textures: procedural canvas 16x16 pixel art, with realistic-ish colors/noise. Build texture atlas 4x4 or 8x8 (16 tiles). Use NearestFilter for crisp cubes, maybe mipmaps for quality. Realistic could use 32x32 textures with subtle noise. Minecraft style = 16x16. We'll generate 16x16 or 32x32 procedural pixel textures with noise and details: grass top, grass side, dirt, stone, cobblestone, sand, oak log side/top, leaves (with transparency), planks, glass, brick, water, snow, gravel, bedrock, glowstone.
- Face culling: skip faces between opaque neighbors; transparent handling: water and leaves and glass need special. Simpler approach: build two geometries per chunk: opaque and transparent. For transparent, cull only same-type neighbors? Water surfaces. Leaves use alphaTest and opaque queue to avoid sorting issues, cull adjacent leaves. Glass alphaTest? Use transparent material. Hmm.

Simplest robust: block definitions with `opaque` bool; for meshing, face is hidden if neighbor is opaque. For transparent blocks, use material with transparent/alphaTest. Leaves: alphaTest material (cutout). Water: transparent material, depthWrite false? If depthWrite false, terrain behind visible. Use separate mesh with transparent material and renderOrder. Water only top surface and sides where neighbor is air/non-water. Fine.

- Vertex ambient occlusion: compute AO for each face vertex based on neighboring blocks (standard 0..3). Multiply color. Also face shading by normal direction. Use MeshLambertMaterial with vertexColors and map. Shadows: DirectionalLight with shadow map covering around player. Chunk meshes cast/receive shadows. Might be expensive but okay with 2048 map and tight frustum. On mobile lower settings.

- Sky: gradient via large inverted box? "only cubes" — sky can be background color + fog; use scene.background color changing over day/night and fog. Sun as cube mesh far away, moon cube, clouds as merged cube clusters slowly moving. Stars as small squares using PointsMaterial (square points = cubes-ish) or instanced tiny cubes. Use InstancedMesh of tiny cubes for stars (e.g., 400) in sky, only visible at night. That's cool and cube-only.

- Terrain gen: 2D value noise with seed, multi-octave. Height = base + hills; water level. Biomes? grass, sand near water, snow at high altitude, stone. Trees: trunk + leaf blob made of cubes. Flowers? small cubes maybe. Caves? not necessary.

- Lighting: hemisphere light + directional sun + ambient. Day/night cycle update sun position, color, fog, sky. Shadows follow player.

- Player: first-person camera, pointer lock on desktop; WASD, shift sprint, space jump, gravity, collision AABB with voxels. Fly mode toggle (double space? key F). On mobile: joystick movement, drag look, jump, fly toggle? Add button.
- Raycast block interaction: voxel DDA raycast up to 8 blocks. Left click break, right click place. Mobile: tap crosshair area to break? Better dedicated buttons: "Break" and "Place" on right side, plus look drag anywhere. Buttons act on crosshair target. Add highlight wireframe cube (BoxHelper? cube line edges) around targeted block.
- Hotbar: 9 slots with block icons rendered as CSS cubes? Could render isometric block icons via canvas (3 faces with texture). Nice. Generate icons in JS using textures drawn in isometric projection. Or simpler: use CSS background images generated from canvas. We'll generate data URLs for block icons with isometric cube drawing.
- Inventory/block picker: "E" opens a creative inventory grid of all blocks. On mobile an inventory button. This is nice for building. Click block to assign to selected hotbar slot.

- Menu visuals: overlay with blurred game background (live world rendered behind), animated. Title "CUBEHAVEN" maybe. Subtitle. Buttons. Responsive. Glassmorphism panels. Font: use system or Google font? Network may be blocked; use local font stack with bold geometric look. Maybe bundle a font? Can't fetch. Use CSS system font + letter-spacing. Could draw logo with CSS 3D cubes? Title with blocky styling (text-shadow).

Menu background: render the world in "cinematic" mode with slow camera orbit, showing terrain. Nice.

- Settings panel: tabs Graphics / Controls / Audio / Game. Sliders styled. Toggle switches. Persist.
  - Render distance 2-6 chunks (perf), shadows on/off, FOV 60-100, brightness, UI scale? Sensitivity, invert Y, sprint toggle, sound volume, music? ambient, day cycle speed, show FPS, clouds.
- Save world: localStorage with seed + edits map (sparse). Autosave every 30s. Buttons Save / New World.

## Objective
- Build a polished 3D Minecraft-style voxel building game using only cubes, with a menu, settings, and responsive support for mobile, tablet, and PC.

## Requirements
- "3D minecraft style game building game realistic only cubes"
- Must include a main menu and settings screen.
- Must adapt to mobile, tablet, and PC.
- User did not specify framework; Three.js was chosen by the assistant.

## Decisions
- Use Three.js + Vite with locally bundled fonts (`@fontsource/silkscreen`, `@fontsource-variable/nunito`).
- Procedurally generated 96×96 island, 48 blocks tall, with ocean, lake, mountain, trees, boulders, day/night cycle, blocky clouds, cube stars, sun/moon cubes.
- Custom chunk meshing with face culling, vertex AO, atlas textures, shadows, optional bloom.
- Creative-only building with 9-slot hotbar and full block library.
- Procedural WebAudio SFX/ambience (no external audio assets).
- LocalStorage saves for world edits/player position/time plus settings and hotbar.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding, `package.json`, Vite setup, Three.js/fonts installed.
- Full HTML UI structure in `index.html`: menu, pause, settings, help, new-world, block library, loading, HUD, touch controls.
- Full responsive CSS in `src/style.css`.
- Procedural texture atlas and isometric block icons in `src/textures.js`.
- Block definitions in `src/blocks.js`.
- Settings persistence/presets in `src/settings.js`.
- Procedural audio manager in `src/audio.js`.
- Voxel world generation, meshing, raycasting, saving edits in `src/world.js`.
- First-person player physics/collision/camera in `src/player.js`.
- HUD/inventory/settings/touch UI logic in `src/ui.js`.
- Main game controller, renderer, sky shader, lighting, clouds, stars, particles, held block, interactions, saves in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- First build/test has not yet been run. Need to verify syntax, runtime, and visuals.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `npm run build` and fix any syntax/build errors.
2. Start the dev/preview server (e.g. `npm run dev` or `npx vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000`) in a persistent session.
3. Use `playwright-cli` to load the page, inspect console errors, screenshot menu, gameplay, settings, and mobile viewport.
4. Verify world generation, player spawn, mining/placing, hotbar, inventory, pause, settings persistence, and touch controls.
5. Visually iterate on lighting/sky/UI quality from screenshots.
6. Confirm `npm run build` produces working `dist/index.html` and all assets.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: game bootstrap, rendering, sky/lighting, interactions, transitions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: voxel generation, chunk meshing, raycast, edits.
